title: Two Tiers are Nice, but...
text:
Two Tiers are Nice, but.... Like most people, I own a dishwasher and rely on it for most of my dishwashing needs. But there is still and will always be a need to wash dishes by hand and therefore a dish rack is a must. I prefer a durable, metal dish rack to the cheaper, plastic varieties and the latest to make its way to my kitchen is the XIGOO Dish Drying Rack.

Two- tier in design, this dish drying rack can handle a moderate number of dishes. The top rack is designed to hold plates while the bottom rack is intended for things that don’t need to be held in place. There is a side attachment for utensils, a second attachment that can hold up to three glasses or cups, and a third attachment that is good for holding a cutting board.

After using this dishrack a few times, I have come away with almost an equal share of pros and cons. I like the draining on the bottom- the water is channeled toward a drain in the center and there is an extension on the bottom that can be directed to the sink. The way it is designed, you can direct this drain in any direction. That means you can place the rack length- wise or sideways and turn the drain extender toward your sink. Having a second tier is nice as well and I like the separate attachment for knives- makes it easy to slip them into their own slot for drying.

Looking at the cons, I have found a few. For one, the dish rack is on the small side. It’s a good thing there is a second tier because the bottom tier is far too small to handle many dishes. Another thing I don’t like is that the utensil holder isn’t positioned to drain into the drip tray. There are holes to release the water, but they end up on the kitchen counter. And the two extension handles on the top rack, while they seem good for hanging a cup, will not allow the cup to dry properly because it won’t be upside down. Thus, these extenders have limited usefulness. Another issue I have is the rack's tendency to slide on the counter. The dish rack itself had non- skid feet, but the drip tray in which it sits doesn't. That means if you use the drip tray- and you almost certainly will want to- you will have to deal with it the possibility of sliding.

If you don’t have too many dishes to dry, the XIGOO Dish Drying Rack could suit your needs. I am undecided on this rack so far, for the reasons listed, and I decided to keep my previous rack within reach in case I decide I like it better and want it back. So, with an almost equal share of good and bad points, I am rating this rack average overall.
